# northflank_preview_blueprint (Resource)

Manages a preview blueprint: the template Northflank runs to create a preview environment, for example for each pull request.

The template is Northflank's JSON template format and is passed through as is, usually with `file()` from the repository Terraform runs in. Terraform delivers it: the blueprint is never linked to the repository through GitOps, so Northflank never writes to it, and a change to the file reaches Northflank on the next apply. A `gitops` key in the template is dropped for the same reason. Changes made to the template in the Northflank dashboard are not detected.

Keep secrets such as webhook trigger tokens out of the template: reference them as `${args.NAME}` and set them in `argument_overrides`, which Northflank stores separately.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The blueprint lives in the application repository as JSON. Terraform reads
# it from the checkout it runs in and delivers it to Northflank, so a change
# to the file takes effect on the next apply, for example from CI on merge.
resource "northflank_preview_blueprint" "pr" {
  project_id = "my-application"
  template   = file("${path.module}/../.northflank/preview-blueprint.json")

  # The template references "${args.WEBHOOK_TOKEN}" in its webhook trigger,
  # so the token itself never goes into the repository.
  argument_overrides = {
    WEBHOOK_TOKEN = random_password.preview_webhook.result
  }
}

resource "random_password" "preview_webhook" {
  length  = 40
  special = false
}

# A CI pipeline can also start runs through the API with this ID:
# POST /v1/projects/my-application/preview-blueprints/<id>/runs
output "preview_blueprint_id" {
  value = northflank_preview_blueprint.pr.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the blueprint belongs to. Changing this forces a new blueprint.
- `template` (String) The blueprint as Northflank's JSON template, with at least `name`, `apiVersion` and `spec`, such as `file("preview-blueprint.json")`.

### Optional

- `argument_overrides` (Map of String, Sensitive) Values for the template's `${args.NAME}` references, stored in Northflank apart from the template, such as a webhook trigger token. Stored in Terraform state; not read back from the API.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the preview blueprint.
- `name` (String) Name of the blueprint, taken from the template. A new name forces a new blueprint.
- `paused` (Boolean) Whether the blueprint's Git and webhook triggers are paused.
- `status` (String) Status of the blueprint's latest run, such as `success` or `running`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Preview blueprints are imported as <project_id>/<preview_blueprint_id>. The
# next apply sends the template and argument overrides from configuration.
terraform import northflank_preview_blueprint.pr my-application/pr-previews
```
